question: What primary classification do condoms hold in family planning?
explanation: Condoms work by physically blocking sperm from reaching an egg, which defines them as a barrier method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h1)

question: What makes condoms different from most other birth control methods?

options.A: They alter the female hormonal cycle
options.B: They offer protection against both pregnancy and STIs

explanation: Dual protection against both infections and conception sets condoms apart from purely hormonal or surgical options. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h1)

question: Which material is most commonly used to make standard male condoms?
explanation: Latex is the most widely utilized material because it offers high elasticity, durability, and affordability. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h2)

question: Where does the inner ring of a female condom rest inside the body?

options.B: Around the base of the penis

explanation: The inner ring helps anchor the device inside the vagina by resting securely near or over the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h2)

question: How do condoms primarily work to prevent pregnancy?
explanation: Condoms act purely through physical occlusion, preventing contact between sperm and egg. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h3)

question: A patient asks how a condom stops sexually transmitted infections. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: It prevents the exchange of infectious bodily fluids
options.B: It neutralizes vaginal acidity to kill germs
options.C: It boosts the immune system against viruses
options.D: It destroys bacteria using built-in antibiotics

explanation: The barrier stops pathogens present in semen and vaginal fluids from passing between sexual partners. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h3)

question: Why must air be squeezed out of the tip when putting on a male condom?

options.B: To help the condom unroll faster
options.C: To make the condom fit tighter
options.D: To prevent the condom from bursting

explanation: Trapped air expands under pressure during ejaculation, causing the latex to rupture if not expelled beforehand. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h4)

question: When should a male condom be put on during sexual activity?

options.A: Before any genital contact takes place

explanation: Pre-ejaculatory fluid can contain sperm and infectious pathogens, requiring barrier placement before any contact. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h4)

question: Which type of lubricant damages latex condoms and should never be used with them?
explanation: Oils break down the chemical bonds in latex rapidly, causing the condom to weaken and tear easily. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h5)

question: What should be done if a condom tears or slips off during intercourse?

options.A: Wash the genital area with soap immediately
options.C: Consider emergency contraception and STI screening options
options.D: Wait two weeks to see if symptoms develop

explanation: Barrier failure requires urgent risk assessment regarding pregnancy prevention and potential exposure to infections. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h5)

question: Which of the following is a major advantage of condoms compared to hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: They require no action during intercourse
options.B: They protect against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Hormonal methods prevent pregnancy effectively but offer no barrier defense against viral or bacterial infections. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h6)

question: What is a main limitation of barrier methods in family planning?

options.B: High cost and complex surgical insertion
options.D: Dependence on correct use during every sexual act

explanation: Because effectiveness depends on proper application every time intercourse occurs, user error or forgetfulness lowers its success rate. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h6)

question: What is an important nursing responsibility during condom counseling sessions?
explanation: Visual and tactile demonstrations help clients grasp correct handling techniques far better than verbal instruction alone. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h7)

question: A young adult client feels embarrassed about asking for condoms at a clinic. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Direct the client to buy them exclusively online
options.B: Scold the client for being irresponsible
options.C: Refuse distribution until the client brings a partner
options.D: Provide a private, non-judgmental space and reassurance

explanation: Creating a welcoming, confidential environment reduces stigma and encourages health-seeking behaviors among young clients. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h7)
